text:
Marla: Anyone know the quickest path to raw request lines given a user-reported X-Request-ID `abcd-4f2`? console hides payload :(
Ben: If you have request_id and a trace, start with the Trace UI to get the span that touched the edge — you'll usually see the pod name. Example: https://console.redwood.ai/traces?query=abcd-4f2
Marla: I don't have a trace id, just the header value from the client's logs
Carla: Grep the edge logs first. On k8s you can `stern` the ingress: `stern -n prod gateway --since 1h | rg \"abcd-4f2\"` if the ingress preserves the header
Ben: if the edge injects the header into upstream, look for `X-Request-ID: abcd-4f2` in proxy logs — that usually surfaces a request span id
Deploy-bot: deploy redwood/gateway v2.14 finished at 1799991200 :rocket:
Marla: got a hit, shows pod `gateway-57f4`. How do I hop to the backend pod logs from there?
Frank: two ways: 1) find the trace/span and follow span.tags to get the upstream pod; 2) search downstream services for the same req id header. The latter via stern/kubectl is fastest for quick debugging.
Emily: CLI snippet I use: `kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=gateway -o name` then `kubectl logs -n prod gateway-57f4 -c gateway --tail 200 | rg \"abcd-4f2\"`
Carla: console Request Explorer is handy too — paste the request id into Request Explorer search (filter `header.request_id:abcd-4f2`) and open the trace to see service hop metadata
Marla: Request Explorer returned trace id `0x9f3c`
Ben: open the trace at: https://console.redwood.ai/traces/0x9f3c — span list shows proxy -> service-a (pod `service-a-2b9`)
Marla: found service-a pod logs, hit the backend request lines. saved the commands for the runbook
Emily: I'll add a short note to the eng-infra runbook about the `X-Request-ID` search flow and the stern pattern :memo:
Ben: also consider adding a small log field `correlation.request_id` in ingress logs so searches are cleaner (and maybe set up a saved query in Console)
Marla: thanks everyone :heart:
